title: Stalk of a direct image of sets as sections over the strict henselization
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $H$ a sheaf of sets on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] with direct image $f_*H$, $(f_*H)(V)=H(V\times_YX)$ for $V$ in $Y_{\Et}$, and $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let $\mathcal N^{\mathrm{aff}}$ be the category of affine pointed etale neighbourhoods $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar y$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods], $V=\operatorname{Spec}A_V$, and let $C=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar y}=\varinjlim_{(V,\bar v)\in\mathcal N^{\mathrm{aff}}}A_V$, $Y^{\mathrm{sh}}=\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with the canonical morphisms $c_V:Y^{\mathrm{sh}}\to V$ (induced by the coprojections $A_V\to C$) and $q:Y^{\mathrm{sh}}\to Y$ (the composite of $c_V$ with $V\to Y$, independent of $V$). Let $X^{\mathrm{sh}}=Y^{\mathrm{sh}}\times_YX$ be the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $f^{\mathrm{sh}}:X^{\mathrm{sh}}\to Y^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $p:X^{\mathrm{sh}}\to X$, let $p^{-1}H$ be the etale inverse image of sheaves of sets and $p^*s\in(p^{-1}H)(W\times_XX^{\mathrm{sh}})$, for $W$ in $X_{\Et}$ and $s\in H(W)$, the image of $s$ under the unit $H\to p_*p^{-1}H$ [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]. For $(V,\bar v)\in\mathcal N^{\mathrm{aff}}$ let $\sigma_V:X^{\mathrm{sh}}\to(V\times_YX)\times_XX^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be the morphism with components $(c_V\circ f^{\mathrm{sh}},p):X^{\mathrm{sh}}\to V\times_YX$ and $\mathrm{id}:X^{\mathrm{sh}}\to X^{\mathrm{sh}}$; it is a morphism of $X^{\mathrm{sh}}_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] from the final object $X^{\mathrm{sh}}$ to the object $(V\times_YX)\times_XX^{\mathrm{sh}}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{pr}_2}X^{\mathrm{sh}}$. Then: (1) every element of the stalk $(f_*H)_{\bar y}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is the germ of a section at an affine pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar y$; (2) there is exactly one map of sets $\Theta:(f_*H)_{\bar y}\to(p^{-1}H)(X^{\mathrm{sh}})$ such that for every $(V,\bar v)\in\mathcal N^{\mathrm{aff}}$ and every $s\in(f_*H)(V)=H(V\times_YX)$, $\Theta(\text{germ of }s\text{ at }(V,\bar v))=(p^{-1}H)(\sigma_V)(p^*s)$; and $\Theta$ is bijective.

proof.text: The structural-map characterization and pullback.condition prove strictHenselizationBaseChange_condition. Use [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-base-change-cone] to obtain the underlying base-changed affine-neighbourhood limit cone with its exact projection formulas.

The chosen small-model pointed-neighbourhood functor is initial by strictHenselization_properties [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Whisker the stalk defining colimit cocone [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] by its opposite final functor. This gives a colimit with the stalk as vertex of precisely the diagram of H on the base-changed neighbourhoods.

Each stage is qcqs because it is the base change of the qcqs morphism f to an affine scheme [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Each neighbourhood transition is affine between affine schemes, and its base change is affine. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-etale-limit-sections] to the cone to get the explicit unit-restriction section colimit with the strict-henselization section set as vertex.

Compare these two colimit cocones by coconePointUniqueUpToIso. The comparison is bijective. Check that its component map is exactly the stated sigma_V restriction of the unit: both site morphisms have identical two outer pullback projections, and their first components have the identical two inner projections given by the geometric cone formulas. Types.jointly_surjective_of_isColimit gives an affine representative for every stalk element. Finally, every competing map agrees on these representatives by its component formula, so function extensionality proves uniqueness.
